vlae.teks: Water wat in een rigting trek en 'n mens kan saamvat, soos in 'n rivier of die see.
vlae.rede: The second half of the relative clause has no repeated 'wat', so a Grade 4 reader can briefly parse "'n mens kan saamvat" as a new main clause (one can take it along) instead of 'which can carry a person away'. Adding 'wat' does not remove the subject/object ambiguity, and this definition was just corrected after a fact check and may be shared, so it is flagged rather than changed; a writer could resolve it with the study text's clearer order (the current carries a person along).

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: kan in water verdrink wat nie tot by sy knieë kom nie
laat_vaar_vorige.na: kan verdrink in water wat nie tot by sy knieë kom nie
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: Putting the relative clause straight after 'water' makes the sentence easier for a Grade 4 reader to follow.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'kan in water verdrink wat ...' is ordinary Afrikaans word order and reads clearly, so the proposal is a lateral move.

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: The bank of a river or dam is a 'wal' in Afrikaans; 'kant' in the plural is vague here.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The paragraph uses 'kant' consistently for the edge, 'walle' of a dam could be read as the dam wall, and the original reads fine.

laat_vaar_vorige.blok: Hoe dit werklik lyk as iemand sukkel
laat_vaar_vorige.voor: In flieks swaai en skreeu die mens wat verdrink.
laat_vaar_vorige.na: In flieks skreeu die mens wat verdrink en swaai hy sy arms.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'swaai' with no object sounds unfinished; the arms are what the verb means, so no content is added.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The original is crisp, and the proposal is longer and invites a misreading of 'wat verdrink en swaai' as one relative clause.

laat_vaar_vorige.blok: Die reëls wat jou veilig hou
laat_vaar_vorige.voor: Loop by die rand en moenie
laat_vaar_vorige.na: Stap by die rand en moenie
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'Stap' makes the contrast with 'hardloop' plain; 'loop by die rand' can also be read as 'go to the edge'.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'Loop' against 'hardloop' is already the natural Afrikaans contrast, so the swap is a lateral move inside a safety rule.

laat_vaar_vorige.blok: As iemand in die moeilikheid is
laat_vaar_vorige.voor: Dit is die eerste ding en die belangrikste ding.
laat_vaar_vorige.na: Dit is die eerste en die belangrikste ding.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: Repeating 'ding' is wooden; the emphasis stays the same without it.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The repeated 'ding' is deliberate emphasis on the first safety action, and removing it weakens that emphasis.

laat_vaar_vorige.na: Om te stoei en iemand in te druk, verander
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: A bare separable verb with an object ('iemand indruk') reads woodenly as a subject; the om-te infinitive is the natural construction and keeps both actions and the meaning.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: A bare infinitive as subject ('Stoei en iemand indruk verander...') is ordinary Afrikaans; the proposal is longer, harder for a Grade 4 reader, and puts a comma between subject and verb inside one sentence, so it is at best a lateral move.

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: For one specific person in a role, 'persoon' is the natural word; 'mens' reads as 'human being' here.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'Die mens wat...' is natural Afrikaans for a person in a role, so swapping it for 'persoon' is a lateral move, and it would reword a shared glossary definition without a real fault.
